question: Find out why white silver chloride turns grey in sunlight.
option_1: Due to rusting of silver in presence of oxygen
option_3: Due to the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light
option_4: Due to the displacement of silver chloride to silver oxide
solution_text:
The correct answer is Due to the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Silver chloride (AgCl) is a photosensitive compound. When exposed to sunlight, it undergoes photolysis (photochemical decomposition), breaking down into metallic silver and chlorine gas. (सिल्वर क्लोराइड — प्रकाश द्वारा अपघटन से चांदी और क्लोरीन)

 

• The reaction is: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ in the presence of sunlight. The finely divided silver deposited on the surface gives the compound its characteristic grey-to-black colour.

 

• This photosensitivity is the basis of traditional black-and-white photography, where silver halides (AgCl, AgBr, AgI) coated on film darken on exposure to light.

 

• The same property is used in photochromic (self-darkening) sunglasses, whose lenses contain silver halide crystals that reversibly darken in sunlight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar light-induced decomposition occurs in silver bromide (AgBr) and silver iodide (AgI), both also used in photographic film.

 

• Silver halides are examples of compounds that undergo photolytic (photochemical) decomposition, a reaction driven directly by light energy rather than heat.

 

NOTE

 

• Due to rusting of silver in presence of oxygen (Option 1): "Rusting" is a term specific to the corrosion of iron; silver does not rust.

 

• Due to redox reaction (Option 2): Though the decomposition does technically involve oxidation-reduction, this option is too vague — the specific, tested reason is the photolytic decomposition of AgCl into Ag and Cl₂ under sunlight.

 

• Due to the displacement of silver chloride to silver oxide (Option 4): No such displacement reaction takes place; AgCl decomposes into elemental silver and chlorine, not silver oxide.

question: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in Calcutta in 1828?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later renamed the Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta in 1828. (ब्रह्म समाज — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• He is widely regarded as the "Father of Modern India" and the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" for his social and religious reform efforts.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj rejected idol worship and preached monotheism based on the Upanishads, and campaigned against social evils such as Sati, child marriage, and caste rigidities.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy's efforts, along with Governor-General Lord William Bentinck, led to the abolition of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Ram Mohan Roy's death, the Brahmo Samaj was reorganised and strengthened by Debendranath Tagore, and later by Keshab Chandra Sen, who eventually split off to form the Brahmo Samaj of India.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy also co-founded the Anglo-Hindu School (1817) with David Hare, and supported the spread of English and Western education in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Swami Vivekanand (Option 2): Founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, a spiritual and philanthropic organisation, not the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 3): A moderate Congress leader who founded the Servants of India Society in 1905; he was Mahatma Gandhi's political mentor.

 

• Ramabai Ranade (Option 4): A social reformer associated with women's education and the Seva Sadan Society, not the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.

question: Which of the following are west flowing rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahi and Sabarmati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahi and Sabarmati are major west-flowing rivers of India that drain into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). (पश्चिम की ओर बहने वाली नदियाँ — माही और साबरमती)

 

• India's main west-flowing river systems are the Narmada, Tapi (Tapti), Mahi, Sabarmati, and several smaller streams of the Western Ghats, all of which drain into the Arabian Sea.

 

• Most Indian rivers, including the Himalayan rivers and a large part of the Peninsular system, are east-flowing, draining into the Bay of Bengal, following the general east/south-eastward slope of the Indian landmass.

 

• The west-flowing Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys/fault troughs, unlike east-flowing peninsular rivers, which follow the natural slope of the land and form deltas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narmada and Tapi are the two largest west-flowing peninsular rivers; unlike most Indian rivers, they form estuaries rather than deltas at their mouths.

 

• East-flowing peninsular rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi form deltas before entering the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Godavari and Mahanadi (Option 1): Both are east-flowing rivers draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Krishna and Kaveri (Option 2): Both are east-flowing peninsular rivers draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Ganga and Yamuna (Option 3): Both belong to the Himalayan river system and flow mainly east/south-east, eventually draining into the Bay of Bengal.

question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution was inserted in the Indian Constitution through _____________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IV-A (Article 51-A), dealing with Fundamental Duties, was inserted into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 42वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम)

 

• The 42nd Amendment was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee and initially added 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th duty (a parent's/guardian's duty to provide education to children aged 6-14) was later added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including adding the words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble.

 

• Fundamental Duties, listed in Part IV-A, are non-justiciable (not directly enforceable by courts) and were inspired by Article 51-A modelled on the Constitution of the former USSR.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment also added Directive Principle Article 39-A (free legal aid) and Article 43-A (workers' participation in management).

 

• Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties) immediately follows Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• 44th Amendment (Option 1): Enacted in 1978, it reversed several changes made by the 42nd Amendment and removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights.

 

• 46th Amendment (Option 2): Relates to changes in Articles 269 and 286, concerning tax on inter-State trade in goods.

 

• 48th Amendment (Option 3): Related to the imposition of President's Rule in Punjab in 1988.

question: Sido and Kanhu were leaders of which of the following tribal rebellions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santhal Rebellion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sido and Kanhu Murmu, two brothers, led the Santhal Rebellion (Santhal Hul) of 1855-56 against British colonial rule and exploitative moneylenders (dikus) in the Rajmahal Hills region (present-day Jharkhand/Bihar). (संथाल विद्रोह — सिदो और कान्हू मुर्मू)

 

• The rebellion arose from oppressive land revenue policies, exploitation by zamindars and moneylenders, and the corrupt colonial administrative-judicial system affecting the Santhal peasantry.

 

• Following the uprising, the British created the separate Santhal Pargana district (1855) to protect Santhal land rights and prevent non-tribal encroachment.

 

• Sido and Kanhu were eventually captured by the British; Sido was executed in 1855.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Murmu siblings involved in the rebellion included brothers Chand and Bhairav, and sisters Phulo and Jhano Murmu.

 

• The Santhal Rebellion is regarded as one of the earliest large-scale organised tribal uprisings against British rule, predating the Revolt of 1857.

 

NOTE

 

• Moplah Rebellion (Option 1): An uprising of Muslim tenants (Mappilas) against Hindu landlords and British rule in Malabar (Kerala), in 1921, associated with leaders such as Ali Musliyar.

 

• Kol Rebellion (Option 3): A tribal uprising in the Chotanagpur region (1831-32), led by figures such as Buddhu Bhagat, against exploitation by outsiders (dikus).

 

• Munda Rebellion (Option 4): Led by Birsa Munda (1899-1900) in the Chotanagpur plateau, also known as the "Ulgulan" (Great Tumult).

question: The outermost part of the Earth is known as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is the crust.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The crust is the outermost and thinnest solid layer of the Earth, lying above the mantle. (भूपर्पटी — पृथ्वी की सबसे बाहरी परत)

 

• The crust is of two types: continental crust (thicker, made mainly of granite/sial) and oceanic crust (thinner, made mainly of basalt/sima).

 

• Below the crust lies the mantle, extending to about 2,900 km in depth; below that lies the core (a liquid outer core and a solid inner core), composed mainly of iron and nickel.

 

• The boundary between the crust and the mantle is called the Mohorovičić Discontinuity (Moho).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The crust makes up less than 1% of Earth's total volume, while the mantle accounts for roughly 84% of it.

 

• Knowledge of Earth's internal layers comes largely from the study of seismic wave behaviour as they pass through the planet.

 

NOTE

 

• Volcano (Option 1): A volcano is a landform/vent in the crust through which molten rock (magma) erupts; it is not a distinct layer of the Earth.

 

• The core (Option 3): The core is the innermost layer of the Earth, not the outermost.

 

• The mantle (Option 4): The mantle lies between the crust and the core; it is not the outermost layer.

question: The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vidhan Parishad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) is the Upper House of a bicameral State Legislature, while the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) is the Lower House. (विधान परिषद — राज्य विधानमंडल का उच्च सदन)

 

• Under Article 169 of the Constitution, a state can create or abolish its Legislative Council through a resolution of its Legislative Assembly, followed by a law passed by Parliament.

 

• Presently, only a few states have a Legislative Council, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

 

• Like the Rajya Sabha, the Vidhan Parishad is a permanent house (not subject to dissolution), with one-third of members retiring every two years, but it has relatively limited legislative powers, especially over money bills.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Members of the Vidhan Parishad are chosen through a mix of methods — election by MLAs, local bodies, teachers' and graduates' constituencies, and nomination by the Governor.

 

• The strength of a Legislative Council cannot exceed one-third of the strength of the Legislative Assembly of that state, subject to a minimum of 40 members.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajya Sabha (Option 2): The Upper House of Parliament at the national level, not of a State Legislature.

 

• Lok Sabha (Option 3): The Lower House of Parliament at the national level.

 

• Vidhan Sabha (Option 4): The Lower House of a State Legislature, not the upper house.

question: According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ annual report (2020-2021), which position does India have in terms of road networks in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Annual Report (2020-21), India has the second largest road network in the world, after the United States. (सड़क नेटवर्क — भारत विश्व में दूसरे स्थान पर)

 

• India's total road network spans over 63 lakh km, comprising National Highways, State Highways, and other district and rural roads.

 

• National Highways, although only about 2% of the total road network, carry roughly 40% of the country's total road traffic.

 

• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways develops and maintains National Highways; Union Minister Nitin Gadkari has repeatedly highlighted India's second-largest road network status.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The United States has the largest road network in the world, followed by India and then China.

 

• Programmes such as Bharatmala Pariyojana aim to further expand and upgrade India's National Highway network.

 

NOTE

 

• First (Option 1): The United States, not India, has the largest road network in the world.

 

• Fourth (Option 3): Incorrect; India ranks second, not fourth, in the world.

 

• Third (Option 4): Incorrect; India ranks second, not third, in the world.

question: Why does the milkman add a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk?
option_1: To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly more acidic
option_2: To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
option_3: To maintain the pH of the fresh milk at 6 for a longer time
option_4: To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
solution_text:
The correct answer is To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fresh milk has a pH of about 6, which is slightly acidic; milkmen add a small amount of baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO₃) to shift this to a slightly alkaline pH. (बेकिंग सोडा — दूध का pH क्षारीय बनाना)

 

• Bacteria in milk produce lactic acid, which lowers the pH over time and eventually causes the milk to curdle; by making the milk slightly alkaline at the outset, this souring/curdling process is delayed.

 

• This allows the milk to stay fresh for a longer duration without curdling, which is useful during storage and transportation before it is pasteurised.

 

• Adding baking soda is a simple preservation trick and is distinct from pasteurisation, which uses controlled heating to kill pathogenic microbes rather than adjust pH.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A red litmus paper turns blue in a basic (alkaline) solution and a blue litmus paper turns red in an acidic one; milk with baking soda added would turn red litmus slightly blue.

 

• Once milk turns fully sour, its pH drops well below 6, causing the milk protein casein to coagulate and curdle.

 

NOTE

 

• To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly more acidic (Option 1): This is the opposite of the intended effect — lowering the pH would speed up curdling, not delay it.

 

• To maintain the pH of the fresh milk at 6 for a longer time (Option 3): Baking soda actively shifts the pH upward (alkaline); it does not simply maintain the original pH of 6.

 

• To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline (Option 4): This is internally contradictory — reducing the pH from 6 would make the milk more acidic, not alkaline; baking soda instead increases the pH.

question: In the context of periodicity, a unit called picometre is used to measure the __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is atomic radius.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Picometre (pm), a very small unit of length (10⁻¹² m), is commonly used to express atomic radius and related periodic properties such as ionic and covalent radii. (पिकोमीटर — परमाणु त्रिज्या की इकाई)

 

• Atomic radius generally decreases across a period (left to right) due to increasing nuclear charge, and increases down a group due to the addition of new electron shells — one of the fundamental periodic trends.

 

• Related quantities such as ionic radius and covalent/van der Waals radius are also commonly expressed in picometres or angstroms (1 Å = 100 pm).

 

• Atomic radius cannot be measured with absolute precision, since an electron cloud has no sharply defined boundary; it is usually estimated from interatomic distances in molecules or crystals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Molar mass is expressed in grams per mole (g/mol), a completely different type of unit from picometre.

 

• Atomic density is typically expressed in g/cm³, and spin quantum number is a dimensionless quantum number (values such as +1/2 or -1/2), not a length.

 

NOTE

 

• Molar mass (Option 2): Measured in g/mol; a mass-per-mole quantity, not a unit of length like the picometre.

 

• Atomic density (Option 3): Measured in mass-per-volume units (e.g., g/cm³), unrelated to the picometre.

 

• Spin quantum number (Option 4): A dimensionless quantum number describing electron spin orientation; it has no unit of length.

question: Who among the following was the Former Secretary (HRD), Information and Broadcasting (I&B) and has been appointed as the advisor to the Prime Minister of India in October 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Khare.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Amit Khare, a retired IAS officer, served as Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and had earlier also held charge related to Higher Education (HRD); he was appointed as an Advisor to the Prime Minister of India in October 2021, after his retirement from service. (अमित खरे — प्रधानमंत्री के सलाहकार)

 

• The Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD) referenced in the question was renamed the Ministry of Education in 2020, and Amit Khare had earlier served as Secretary, Department of Higher Education under it.

 

• As Advisor to the PM, he has been associated with policy matters relating to information, education and skill development within the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

 

• He was subsequently granted an extension as Advisor to Prime Minister Narendra Modi beyond his initial term.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD) was renamed the Ministry of Education as part of the reforms under the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020.

 

• Advisors and Officers on Special Duty (OSDs) at the PMO assist the Prime Minister on specific policy domains and are typically drawn from senior retired or serving bureaucrats.

 

NOTE

 

• Shri Apurva Chandra (Option 1): An IAS officer who went on to serve as Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, but he is not the officer who was appointed Advisor to the PM in October 2021.

 

• PK Sinha (Option 2): A former Cabinet Secretary of India who also served as Principal Advisor to the PM, but he is not the former I&B/HRD Secretary described in the question.

 

• Amarjeet Sinha (Option 3): A retired IAS officer who served as Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, not as I&B Secretary.

question: Harrod Domar model was the main idea behind the __________ Five Year Plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is First.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model, which relates savings, the capital-output ratio, and economic growth. (हैरोड-डोमर मॉडल — पहली पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The First Plan focused mainly on agriculture, irrigation and power projects (e.g., the Bhakra Nangal, Damodar Valley and Hirakud dams), and India achieved a growth rate higher than its target during this period.

 

• The Harrod-Domar model, developed independently by economists Roy Harrod and Evsey Domar, is a capital-driven growth model, distinct from the more industry-focused Mahalanobis model used later.

 

• In contrast, the Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the P. C. Mahalanobis model, which emphasised rapid industrialisation, particularly heavy and basic industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission of India was established in 1950, and Five Year Plans were formulated under its aegis until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

 

• India's Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) was the last of the series before the Five Year Plan system was discontinued.

 

NOTE

 

• Third Five Year Plan (Option 1): Aimed at making the economy "self-reliant" and self-generating; it was adversely affected by the Indo-China War (1962) and Indo-Pak War (1965).

 

• Second Five Year Plan (Option 3): Based on the Mahalanobis model, it focused on rapid industrialisation and the growth of public sector/heavy industries.

 

• Fourth Five Year Plan (Option 4): Based on the Gadgil strategy, with the twin objectives of "growth with stability" and progress towards self-reliance.

question: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in 2008 to provide health insurance coverage to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families. (राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना — 2008)

 

• RSBY offered cashless health insurance cover of up to ₹30,000 per year on a family-floater basis for BPL households, covering hospitalisation expenses.

 

• The scheme used a smart card-based system, allowing beneficiaries to avail cashless treatment at empanelled public and private hospitals across India.

 

• RSBY was later subsumed into Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), launched in 2018, which significantly raised the coverage amount to ₹5 lakh per family per year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• RSBY was transferred from the Ministry of Labour and Employment to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2015.

 

• Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY, launched on 23 September 2018, is now the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• 2017 (Option 1): No major national BPL health insurance scheme was launched in this year; Ayushman Bharat was announced in the 2018 Budget and launched later that September.

 

• 2009 (Option 2): RSBY had already been launched a year earlier, in 2008, not 2009.

 

• 2014 (Option 3): RSBY predates this year, having been launched in 2008.

question: Money supply is a _____ concept.
solution_text:
The correct answer is stock.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Money supply is a stock concept, meaning it is measured at a specific point in time (e.g., total money in circulation on a given date), unlike a flow that is measured over a period. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति — स्टॉक अवधारणा)

 

• In economics, a stock variable (like wealth, capital, or money supply) has no time dimension attached to it, while a flow variable (like income, expenditure, or investment) is measured per unit of time.

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) measures and publishes money supply through different monetary aggregates — M1, M2, M3 and M4 — based on liquidity, each representing the stock of money held at a point in time.

 

• M3 (broad money) is the most commonly used measure of money supply in India, comprising currency with the public, demand deposits, and time deposits with banks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• National income and GDP are classic examples of flow concepts, since they are measured over a specific time period, such as a financial year.

 

• Wealth and capital are other common examples of stock variables in economics, similar to money supply.

 

NOTE

 

• Measurable (Option 2) and Non-measurable (Option 3): These describe whether a quantity can be numerically quantified, not the stock/flow classification being tested; money supply is, in fact, a measurable quantity, so Option 3 is doubly incorrect.

 

• Flow (Option 4): This is the opposite classification — money supply is a stock concept, since it is measured at a point in time rather than over a period.

question: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On Republic Day (26 January), the Governor of each state unfurls the National Flag at the state capital, as the constitutional head of the state. (गणतंत्र दिवस — राज्यपाल द्वारा ध्वजारोहण)

 

• In contrast, on Independence Day (15 August), the Chief Minister (as the head of government) hoists the flag at the state level, while the Prime Minister hoists it at the Red Fort, Delhi.

 

• At the national level on Republic Day, the flag-hoisting and main parade are presided over by the President of India at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), New Delhi.

 

• This distinction — the Governor hoisting the flag on Republic Day and the Chief Minister on Independence Day — is a frequently tested point of state-level ceremonial protocol.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Governor is appointed by the President of India under Article 155 and holds office during the President's pleasure, acting as the nominal/constitutional head of the state executive under Article 154.

 

• The Chief Minister, as the real executive head of the state, hoists the flag on Independence Day and presides over most other state functions.

 

NOTE

 

• Judge of High Court (Option 1): No flag-hoisting role on Republic Day at the state level is assigned to High Court judges.

 

• Chief Minister (Option 2): The Chief Minister unfurls the flag on Independence Day, not Republic Day.

 

• Speaker (Option 4): The Speaker presides over the Legislative Assembly; flag-hoisting on Republic Day at the state capital is a gubernatorial, not a legislative, function.

question: Who among the following is one of the Deputy Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh as of July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Keshav Prasad Maurya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Keshav Prasad Maurya is one of the two Deputy Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh, serving under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in the Second Yogi Adityanath Ministry formed after the 2022 UP Assembly elections. (उत्तर प्रदेश उपमुख्यमंत्री — केशव प्रसाद मौर्य)

 

• The other Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, as of July 2023, is Brajesh Pathak.

 

• Yogi Adityanath has served as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh since 2017 and was re-elected for a consecutive second term in 2022, becoming the first UP Chief Minister to do so.

 

• Both Deputy Chief Ministers belong to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which governs Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttar Pradesh is India's most populous state and sends the largest number of members (80) to the Lok Sabha.

 

• The post of Deputy Chief Minister is not a constitutional office; it is a political/administrative designation without special constitutional powers beyond that of a regular minister.

 

NOTE

 

• Narottam Mishra (Option 1): A senior BJP leader from Madhya Pradesh, not Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Yogi Adityanath (Option 2): He is the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, not a Deputy Chief Minister.

 

• Manoj Sinha (Option 3): The Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, not a Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.

question: Who among the following is/was a famous sitarist?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a globally renowned Indian classical musician and sitar maestro, credited with popularising Indian classical music, especially the sitar, in the Western world. (सितार वादक — रवि शंकर)

 

• He was conferred India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999, and won three Grammy Awards during his lifetime.

 

• He collaborated with Western musicians such as George Harrison of The Beatles and violinist Yehudi Menuhin, significantly boosting global interest in Indian classical music.

 

• His daughters, Anoushka Shankar (sitarist) and Norah Jones (singer), have also had notable music careers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ravi Shankar founded the Kinnara School of Music in Mumbai (1962) and was also a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha (1986-1992).

 

• Other celebrated Indian sitarists include Ustad Vilayat Khan and Pandit Nikhil Banerjee.

 

NOTE

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (Option 2): A legendary shehnai player, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, not a sitarist.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Option 3): A renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, not a sitarist.

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 4): A world-renowned tabla player, son of tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha, not a sitarist.

question: Three Poets Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called as the ‘Three Jewels’ of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kannada Literature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pampa, Ponna, and Ranna are collectively known as the "Three Gems/Jewels" (Ratnatraya) of Kannada literature, all associated with courts of the Chalukya/Rashtrakuta period. (तीन रत्न — कन्नड़ साहित्य)

 

• Pampa (10th century CE) is regarded as the "Father of Kannada poetry" (Adikavi), known for works such as Vikramarjuna Vijaya (Pampa Bharata) and Adipurana.

 

• Ponna was a court poet of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III and authored Shanti Purana, earning the title "Ubhaya Kavichakravarthi" (emperor of poets in two languages — Kannada and Sanskrit).

 

• Ranna was a court poet of the Western Chalukya kings Tailapa II and later Satyashraya; his major work is Gadayuddha (Sahasa Bhima Vijaya), and he held the title "Kavichakravarthi".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• These three poets belong to the early period of Kannada literature, largely composed in the Champu style, which blends prose and verse.

 

• Kannada is one of the classical languages of India, a status conferred in recognition of its ancient and rich literary tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Telugu Literature (Option 2): The "Trinity" of Telugu literature (translators of the Mahabharata into Telugu) are Nannaya, Tikkana, and Yerrapragada (Errana), not Pampa, Ponna and Ranna.

 

• Tamil Literature (Option 3): Ancient Tamil literature developed through the Sangam period and is associated with different celebrated works and poets.

 

• Sanskrit Literature (Option 4): Pampa, Ponna and Ranna wrote primarily in Kannada, and are specifically celebrated as gems of Kannada, not Sanskrit, literature.

question: Indian classical violinist Annavarapu Rama Swamy was awarded with the _____________ in 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annavarapu Rama Swamy, an eminent Indian classical (Carnatic) violinist, was conferred the Padma Shri award in 2021 for his contribution to art and music. (पद्म श्री — अन्नावरपु रामस्वामी)

 

• The Padma Awards are among India's highest civilian honours, announced annually on the eve of Republic Day, and are given in three categories in descending order of distinction: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

• Padma Awards are conferred by the President of India in fields such as art, literature, science, sports, public affairs and social work.

 

• Musicians from Andhra Pradesh, including Annavarapu Rama Swamy, have been recognised through the Padma Awards for preserving classical Carnatic music traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day (26 January).

 

• The awards are given without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex, and are generally not conferred posthumously except in exceptional circumstances.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi (Option 2): This refers to the separate Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar), given by India's national academy for music, dance and drama, distinct from the Padma Awards.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 3): This is the second-highest civilian award, a higher category than the one Annavarapu Rama Swamy actually received in 2021.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 4): This is the third-highest civilian award, again a higher category than the Padma Shri he was actually awarded.

question: Under which of the following Acts, the Board of Control was established in England to control and supervise the administration of British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pitt’s India Act of 1784.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Board of Control was established in England under Pitt's India Act of 1784 to supervise and control the political and administrative affairs of the East India Company in India, introducing a system of dual control over Company rule. (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट 1784 — बोर्ड ऑफ कंट्रोल)

 

• Under this system, the Court of Directors of the Company continued to manage commercial affairs, while the Board of Control, appointed by the British Crown, supervised political, civil and military matters — subordinating Company rule to government oversight.

 

• This Act marked the first time the British Government formally assumed a direct role in overseeing the administration of British India, going a step beyond the earlier Regulating Act of 1773.

 

• The dual system created by Pitt's India Act continued, with modifications, until the Government of India Act, 1858, which abolished Company rule entirely after the Revolt of 1857.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step towards British parliamentary control over the East India Company's affairs, creating the office of Governor-General of Bengal (first holder: Warren Hastings).

 

• The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over Indian trade (except tea and trade with China), opening India's trade to other British merchants.

 

NOTE

 

• Charter Act of 1813 (Option 1): Ended the East India Company's monopoly over Indian trade (except tea and the China trade); it did not establish the Board of Control.

 

• Regulating Act of 1773 (Option 2): Created the post of Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court at Calcutta; the Board of Control came later, under the 1784 Act.

 

• Charter Act of 1793 (Option 3): Mainly renewed the Company's charter and trade privileges for a further 20 years, without establishing the Board of Control.

question: Which of the following states was the overall champion in both men and women categories in the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Odisha emerged as the overall champion in both the men's and women's categories in the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, held in Bhubaneswar in June 2023. (जनजातीय खेल महोत्सव — ओडिशा)

 

• The event was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, in partnership with KIIT and KISS University, Bhubaneswar, to promote sporting talent among tribal youth from across India.

 

• The Mahotsav featured a mix of traditional/indigenous tribal sports and mainstream athletic disciplines, bringing together tribal athletes from various states and Union Territories.

 

• The event aims to provide a platform to nurture and showcase the sporting talent of tribal communities, in line with the broader Khelo India initiative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs also runs schemes such as Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) to support tribal students, including in sports.

 

• Khelo India is the Government of India's flagship programme for the grassroots-level development of sports across the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Did not emerge as the overall champion of the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 2): A state with a significant tribal population, but it was not the overall champion of this event.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Also has a large tribal population, but Odisha, not Jharkhand, won the overall championship.

question: According to the Varna system that was prevalent in the Vedic period, which of the following was NOT a Varna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samiti.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Varna system in Vedic society comprised four varnas: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra; "Samiti" was not a varna but a Vedic tribal assembly. (सभा और समिति — वैदिक सभाएँ, वर्ण नहीं)

 

• Sabha and Samiti were the two important political/tribal assemblies of the Rigvedic period, functioning as deliberative or advisory bodies, sometimes involved in matters relating to the tribal chief (rajan).

 

• The Brahmanas (priests/teachers), Kshatriyas (warriors/rulers), and Vaishyas (traders/agriculturists/cattle-rearers), along with the Shudras (service providers), formed the fourfold Varna classification described in later Vedic texts such as the Purusha Sukta of the Rigveda.

 

• Over time, the Varna system, originally described in terms of occupation, became increasingly rigid and hereditary, gradually evolving into the later caste (jati) system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Purusha Sukta hymn (Rigveda, 10th Mandala) describes the symbolic origin of the four varnas from the body of the cosmic being Purusha — the Brahmana from the mouth, the Kshatriya from the arms, the Vaishya from the thighs, and the Shudra from the feet.

 

• The Sabha is believed to have been a smaller, more select assembly (possibly of elders), while the Samiti was a larger general assembly of the tribe.

 

NOTE

 

• Brahmanas (Option 1): One of the four recognised Varnas, representing priests and teachers.

 

• Kshatriyas (Option 2): One of the four recognised Varnas, representing warriors and rulers.

 

• Vaishyas (Option 4): One of the four recognised Varnas, representing traders, agriculturists, and cattle-rearers.

question: Who was the first Indian woman wrestler to represent the country at the 2012 London Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geeta Phogat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Geeta Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to qualify for and represent India at the Olympic Games, competing in the 55 kg freestyle category at the 2012 London Olympics. (गीता फोगाट — पहली भारतीय महिला पहलवान, लंदन ओलंपिक 2012)

 

• She is the eldest daughter of wrestling coach Mahavir Singh Phogat and belongs to the famous Phogat wrestling family of Haryana, whose story inspired the Bollywood film Dangal (2016).

 

• Geeta Phogat had earlier won a gold medal at the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi in the 55 kg freestyle category, becoming the first Indian woman wrestler to win a Commonwealth gold.

 

• Her sisters/cousins, including Babita Phogat and Vinesh Phogat, are also accomplished international wrestlers who went on to represent India at later Olympic Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sakshi Malik became the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal, a bronze at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

 

• Vinesh Phogat represented India at the 2016 (Rio), 2020 (Tokyo) and 2024 (Paris) Olympics, and reached the final of the 2024 Paris Olympics before being disqualified on a weight technicality.

 

NOTE

 

• Babita Phogat (Option 1): An accomplished wrestler and Commonwealth Games gold medallist, but she represented India at the 2016 Rio Olympics, not the 2012 London Olympics.

 

• Sakshi Malik (Option 2): Competed at the 2016 Rio Olympics, where she won India's first Olympic wrestling medal by a woman; she did not compete at the 2012 London Olympics.

 

• Vinesh Phogat (Option 3): Made her Olympic debut at the 2016 Rio Olympics, not the 2012 London Olympics.

question: Which marine carotenoid is abundant in brown seaweed, macroalgae and diatoms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fucoxanthin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fucoxanthin is a marine carotenoid pigment found abundantly in brown seaweed (brown algae), macroalgae, and diatoms, giving them their characteristic brown/olive colouration. (फ्यूकोक्सैंथिन — भूरे समुद्री शैवाल का रंगद्रव्य)

 

• It is a type of xanthophyll that plays a role in photosynthesis, helping capture light energy in the blue-green wavelength range, which is important for algae living in deeper or turbid waters.

 

• Fucoxanthin has been widely studied for potential health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-obesity, and anti-inflammatory properties, and is used in nutraceutical/dietary supplements.

 

• It masks the green colour of the chlorophyll present in brown algae, which is why brown seaweeds appear brown or golden rather than green.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diatoms are microscopic, single-celled algae with silica-based cell walls, forming a major part of marine phytoplankton and contributing significantly to global oxygen production.

 

• Common carotenoids and their sources include: beta-carotene (carrots), lycopene (tomatoes), lutein (leafy greens), and astaxanthin (salmon, shrimp, algae).

 

NOTE

 

• Astaxanthin (Option 2): A red-orange carotenoid found in salmon, shrimp, krill and certain microalgae (such as Haematococcus pluvialis), not primarily in brown seaweed.

 

• Neoxanthin (Option 3): A xanthophyll pigment found mainly in green plants and leafy vegetables as part of their photosynthetic pigment system, not characteristic of brown seaweed.

 

• β-cryptoxanthin (Option 4): A carotenoid commonly found in fruits such as oranges, papaya and peaches, not specifically associated with brown seaweed/diatoms.

question: The Parliament passed the Essential Defence Services Bill, 2021 in August 2021. Which of the following is an objective behind passing it?
option_1: To encourage more FDI in defence services
option_2: To prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units engaged in essential defence services
option_3: To appoint more women in defence services
option_4: To implement one rank one pension
solution_text:
The correct answer is To prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units engaged in essential defence services.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Essential Defence Services Act, 2021 (passed as a Bill in August 2021) empowers the central government to declare certain services related to defence production/establishments as "essential defence services" and to prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units providing such services. (आवश्यक रक्षा सेवा अधिनियम 2021 — हड़ताल पर प्रतिबंध)

 

• The Act was introduced in the context of the corporatisation of the Ordnance Factory Board (OFB), to ensure the uninterrupted supply of defence equipment and ammunition to the armed forces even as the OFB was restructured into new Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs).

 

• Violation of the Act's provisions, such as participating in a prohibited strike, can attract penalties including imprisonment and/or fines for persons/employees in essential defence service units.

 

• The Act aims to safeguard national security and defence preparedness by ensuring the continuous functioning of units critical to defence production.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ordnance Factory Board (OFB), formerly a subordinate office of the Ministry of Defence, was corporatised in October 2021 into seven new DPSUs, including Munitions India Limited and Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited, among others.

 

• The Act followed protests and apprehensions among employee federations of ordnance factories regarding the corporatisation move.

 

NOTE

 

• To encourage more FDI in defence services (Option 1): FDI-related defence sector reforms are governed by separate FDI policy notifications, not by the Essential Defence Services Act, 2021.

 

• To appoint more women in defence services (Option 3): This Act does not deal with recruitment or gender representation in the defence forces.

 

• To implement one rank one pension (Option 4): OROP (One Rank One Pension) is a separate, distinct policy for defence pensioners, unrelated to this Act.
